status: retained: remove resident normalization broadcasts and use resident one-row replay
platform: Dedicated gfx1151 Strix Halo, Linux x86-64, Nix release. No power or clock changes.
artifact_reference: dflash2-rollback.json: artifacts.target_q4, target_q8 and draft_q4; unchanged files.
change: FP32 resident recurrence repeats the ordered four-wave norm sum locally, removing the key/query norm broadcast barrier and the post-output RMS broadcast barrier. The existing barriers protecting shared key storage, state updates and transitions between rows remain.

For 128x128 FP32 state, one-row state-only replay now uses the existing 128-thread resident specialization. Scalar output-producing AR stays on the generic 256-thread path. BF16 storage and other dimensions retain the generic path.

All sums, state-update FMA ordering, normalization operations, storage, copied bytes, draft, sampler and controller are unchanged. The existing standalone recurrence ablation selects the new one-row replay dispatch. No new maintained tool, test executable or execution switch.

speed.method: Q4 target/Q4 draft, C1, greedy. Adaptive raw JSON/prose TG300: two timed samples per binary in ABBA order, 128-token raw prose warmup per binary excluded. Fixed-7 repetition chat TG128: two paired samples per binary in ABBA order. Includes prefill, excludes model loading. All IDs and acceptance statistics checked against qualified AR references. Candidate removes resident normalization broadcasts and selects resident FP32 state-only replay for one row. Scalar AR, ordered arithmetic, storage, draft, and controller are unchanged. Repetition initial two samples were flat (-0.13%) with one low candidate sample; a second ABBA block checks the possible regression. All eight repetition measurements remain included in the pooled four-per-binary result.

profile.method: One candidate prose TG300 diagnostic trace. Baseline reuses the immediately preceding qualified189b402 trace from /tmp/qwen-state-copy-release/profile.json. Identical Q4/Q4 artifacts, raw prompt, greedy adaptive controller, IDs and acceptance counts. GPU timings are attribution, not throughput.

microbenchmark.method: Actual production template versus pinned 189b402 generic and resident kernels. FP32 48-head/16-key-head, 128x128 state. Eight sequential updates with changing full-mantissa inputs compare every output/state bit before timing. Eight balanced rounds x192 launches, rotating 48 layers (144MiB), identical state reset outside measured region. Seed1 for final production variant; preliminary one-row probe used seeds1/971 and broadcast probe seed971.

limits: Short fresh ABBA controls, including prefill and excluding loading. Prose/JSON use two samples per binary; repetition uses four, including every initial and follow-up sample. No full depth sweep or confidence-interval claim.

The profile reuses the immediately preceding qualified 189b402 trace as baseline and profiles only the candidate; use fresh unprofiled timings for total throughput. The production microbenchmarks separately cover verification widths 3, 5, 8 and replay width 1.

Generic scalar AR remains the model-test reference. Q4/Q8 full-logit, feature, cache, rollback, replay and logical 262144 short-prefix controls passed. The existing SSM suite covers both FP32/BF16. Unchanged draft operator/sampling/HTTP/depth suites were not repeated.
Original checkpoint/conversion and MTP quality qualification, the complete speed matrix and C>1 serving throughput remain separate open work. The 75-question capability comparison has not run.
The original FP4 headline 65.6 JSON/26.1 prose decode-only remains unmatched; matched-Kquant results and the everyday 55 figure do not replace that goal.
